title: Where Clauses for Readable Bounds
goal: Move complex trait bounds out of function parameter lists using where clauses.

sections.text: In languages with generics like Java or C++, long type bounds make function signatures hard to scan.

sections.caption: Inline bounds work well when the signature is short.

sections.text: When functions have multiple generic parameters or several bounds per type, inline syntax grows cluttered.
Rust offers where clauses to separate generic types from their constraints.

sections.code:
fn show<T, U>(title: T, val: U) -> String
where
    T: std::fmt::Display,
    U: std::fmt::Debug,
{
    format!("{title}: {val:?}")
}
sections.caption: where comes after the return type and before the body block.

sections.text: A where clause is purely syntactic layout. It expresses the exact same bounds as inline syntax without cluttering parameter lists.

explanation: Move complex trait bounds out of function parameter lists using where clauses.
